A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the use of a full posterior distribution of ASR hypotheses is a powerful approach for SLU, and that this can be combined with a discriminative training approach.

the use of the full posterior recognition output distribution can significantly improve the performance of a dialogue system, and that the system is robust enough to handle the errors that occur in a live dialogue trial.

we have developed a robust and efficient method for Spoken Language understanding that is able to operate on the full posterior distribution output by a state-of-the-art ASR system and that is able to achieve a significant improvement over a baseline grammar-based approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the full posterior distribution output by a speech recogniser can be used for SLU in a discriminative manner, without the need for hand-crafted grammatical models.
the ASR output distribution, when encoded as a word confusion network, can be used for discriminative SLU, achieving performance comparable to or better than that of a grammar-based approach.
robust spoken language understanding can be achieved by operating directly on the full posterior recognition hypothesis distribution.
